quizzes.title: Vectors, Dot and Cross Products, and Matrices

questions.q: Two nonzero vectors are perpendicular exactly when what is true? [1.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.4: The dot product equals |A||B| cos θ, and cos 90° = 0.
B is wrong: A zero cross product means the vectors are parallel.
C is wrong: Length says nothing about angle.
D is wrong: That depends on their lengths; perpendicular needs zero.

questions.q: A constant force F acts along a displacement d. What work does it do? [1.5]
options: F · d, the dot product of force and displacement
The determinant of F and d
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.5: Only the component of force along the motion does work, which the dot product picks out.
A is wrong: That is a vector, and it is the form used for torque, not work.
C is wrong: The cosine of the angle matters; a sideways force does no work.
D is wrong: A determinant gives an area, not work.

questions.q: What is the length of the cross product A × B? [1.7]
options: |A||B| sin θ, the area of the parallelogram A and B span
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.7: The cross product's length is the parallelogram's area, and its direction is perpendicular to both vectors.
A is wrong: That is the dot product.
B is wrong: Lengths do not simply add in a product.
C is wrong: It is zero only for parallel vectors.

questions.q: For A = (1, 2, 0) and B = (3, 1, 0), what is A × B? [1.9]
options: (0, 0, −5), pointing straight down the z axis
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.9: The k component is 1·1 − 2·3 = −5; the i and j components are zero because both vectors lie in the xy plane.
B is wrong: The sign is wrong: 1·1 − 2·3 is −5.
C is wrong: 5 is the dot product; the cross product is a vector.
D is wrong: That is the componentwise product, which is not the cross product.

questions.q: If a 3 × 3 matrix A has determinant zero, what can be said about A x = b? [1.12]
options: It always has exactly one solution
It has either no solution or infinitely many
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.12: Zero determinant means the rows lie in one plane, so the system is degenerate.
A is wrong: That is the case when the determinant is not zero.
C is wrong: Linear systems never have exactly two solutions.
D is wrong: A has no inverse when its determinant is zero.

quizzes.title: Lines, Planes, and Curves in Space

questions.q: What determines a plane in space, in the lecture's description? [2.2]
options: A single direction vector lying in the plane
One point on the plane and a normal vector perpendicular to it
Its distance from the origin alone
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.2: A point P lies on the plane exactly when the vector from P₀ to P is perpendicular to N.
A is wrong: Two points fix only a line.
B is wrong: Infinitely many planes contain a given direction.
D is wrong: Many planes share the same distance from the origin.

questions.q: How do you find a normal vector to the plane through three given points? [2.3]
options: Take the dot product of two of the points
Form two vectors from one point to the other two and take their cross product
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.3: The cross product is perpendicular to both vectors, and so to the plane.
A is wrong: The sum is not perpendicular to the plane in general.
B is wrong: A dot product is a number, not a vector.
C is wrong: That gives a point, not a normal direction.

questions.q: What is the speed of a moving point along a curve r(t)? [2.7]
options: The length of the velocity vector dr/dt
The length of the position vector
The length of the acceleration vector
The arc length divided by the radius
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.7: Velocity is the derivative of position; its length is the speed ds/dt.
B is wrong: That is the distance from the origin.
C is wrong: Acceleration measures change of velocity.
D is wrong: That has no general meaning as speed.

questions.q: For uniform motion on a circle of radius a with angular speed ω, what is the acceleration? [2.9]
options: Zero, because the speed is constant
It points along the velocity with size a ω
It points away from the centre with size ω
It points toward the centre with size a ω², the speed squared over the radius
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.9: Differentiating twice gives −ω² times the position vector.
A is wrong: The direction of the velocity is turning, so acceleration is not zero.
B is wrong: a ω is the speed, and the acceleration is perpendicular to the velocity.
C is wrong: It points inward, and its size is a ω².

questions.q: What does Kepler's second law follow from, in the lecture's vector account? [2.11]
options: The dot product of position and velocity is zero
The cross product of position and velocity is constant under a force directed toward the Sun
The speed of the planet is constant
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.11: Half its length is the rate of sweeping out area, so equal areas are swept in equal times.
A is wrong: That would mean a circular orbit only.
C is wrong: Planets move faster when nearer the Sun.
D is wrong: Gravity accelerates the planet toward the Sun.

quizzes.title: Functions of Several Variables and Partial Derivatives

questions.q: What is the partial derivative ∂f/∂x? [3.3]
options: The ordinary derivative of f in x while the other variables are held constant
The derivative of f along the steepest direction
The total change in f over a region
The derivative with all variables changing at once
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.3: Geometrically it is the slope of the surface as you walk in the x direction.
B is wrong: That is the length of the gradient.
C is wrong: That is an integral, not a derivative.
D is wrong: A partial derivative changes one variable at a time.

questions.q: A plate measured as 2 m by 3 m has a 1 cm error in each side. About how much does the area estimate change? [3.5]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.5: ΔA ≈ y Δx + x Δy = 3(0.01) + 2(0.01) = 0.05 m².
A is wrong: That is only the product of the two small errors, which the linear estimate ignores.
B is wrong: The partials are 3 and 2, not 3 and 3.
D is wrong: The decimal place is off by a factor of ten.

questions.q: What is z = x² − y² an example of at the origin? [3.7]
options: A saddle: a critical point that is neither a maximum nor a minimum
A point where the partials are not zero
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.7: Both partials are zero there, but the surface rises in one direction and falls in another.
A is wrong: It decreases along the y direction.
B is wrong: It increases along the x direction.
D is wrong: Both partials vanish at the origin.

questions.q: In the second derivative test, what does A C − B² < 0 mean at a critical point? [3.8]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.8: A negative value of A C − B² means a saddle; a positive value means a maximum or minimum, decided by the sign of A.
A is wrong: That needs A C − B² > 0 and A > 0.
B is wrong: That needs A C − B² > 0 and A < 0.
D is wrong: That is the case when A C − B² = 0.

questions.q: For an open-topped box of fixed volume using the least material, what shape does the lecture find? [3.10]
options: A square base with height equal to twice the side
A very flat box with tiny height
A square base with height half the side of the base
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.10: Setting both partial derivatives of the area to zero gives that proportion.
A is wrong: A cube is best for a closed box, not an open-topped one.
B is wrong: The height is half the side, not twice it.
C is wrong: That uses too much material in the base.

quizzes.title: The Gradient, the Chain Rule, and Lagrange Multipliers

questions.q: What is the gradient of f(x, y) = x² + y² at the point (x, y)? [4.2]
options: (2x, 2y), pointing straight away from the origin
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.2: The gradient's components are the partial derivatives f_x and f_y.
A is wrong: Those are the terms, not their derivatives.
C is wrong: The gradient is a vector, not a sum.
D is wrong: The components are swapped.

questions.q: How is the gradient related to the level curves and level surfaces of f? [4.4]
options: It is parallel to the z axis
It has no fixed relation to them
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.4: Along a level set f does not change, so the gradient dotted with any tangent velocity is zero.
A is wrong: Moving along a level set gives zero rate of change, so the gradient cannot point that way.
B is wrong: The gradient lies in the domain, not along the height axis.
C is wrong: The chain rule gives a definite relation.

questions.q: In which direction is the directional derivative of f largest? [4.5]
options: Along the gradient, where it equals the length of the gradient
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.5: The directional derivative is |∇f| cos of the angle, largest when the angle is zero.
A is wrong: There the directional derivative is zero.
B is wrong: That is the direction of fastest decrease.
C is wrong: The best direction depends on the function and the point.

questions.q: What condition does the method of Lagrange multipliers impose to find extremes of f subject to g = constant? [4.8]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.8: At a constrained extreme, the gradient of f is a multiple of the gradient of g.
B is wrong: That ignores the constraint and finds unconstrained critical points.
C is wrong: The gradients are parallel, not perpendicular.
D is wrong: The method compares gradients, not function values.

questions.q: What point on the line x + y = 1 is closest to the origin? [4.10]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.10: Lagrange's condition gives x = y, and the constraint then gives x = y = 1/2.
A is wrong: That point is on the line but at distance 1.
C is wrong: The origin is not on the line.
D is wrong: That point is not on the line.

quizzes.title: Double Integrals, Line Integrals, and Green's Theorem

questions.q: What is the volume under z = x + y over the unit square 0 ≤ x, y ≤ 1? [5.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.4: The inner integral gives x + 1/2, and integrating that from 0 to 1 gives 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.
A is wrong: That is only half the answer: it forgets one of the two equal contributions.
B is wrong: The integrand averages to 1 over the square, so the volume is 1.
D is wrong: That is not the value of the iterated integral.

questions.q: What is the small area element in polar coordinates? [5.5]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.5: A small polar box has sides dr and r dθ.
A is wrong: This omits the factor r, the most common error.
C is wrong: The extra factor is r, not r².
D is wrong: The conversion multiplies by r; it does not divide.

questions.q: When is a vector field conservative, or path independent? [5.10]
options: Only when it is zero everywhere
Exactly when it is the gradient of a potential function
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.10: Then the work along any path is the difference of the potential between the endpoints.
A is wrong: Zero divergence is about sources and sinks, not path independence.
B is wrong: Constant magnitude does not make work path independent.
C is wrong: Many non-zero fields, such as gravity, are conservative.

questions.q: In a simply connected region, what test shows that M i + N j is a gradient field? [5.11]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.11: The difference of those partials is the curl in the plane; zero curl in a region with no holes means conservative.
A is wrong: That compares the wrong partials.
B is wrong: Equal components do not make a field conservative.
D is wrong: That is zero divergence, not zero curl.

questions.q: Using Green's theorem, what is the circulation of −y i + x j around the unit circle? [5.12]
options: 2π, because the curl is 2 and the disc's area is π
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.12: The double integral of the curl, 2, over the unit disc equals 2π, matching the direct line integral.
A is wrong: This forgets that the curl is 2, not 1.
B is wrong: The field circulates, so the circulation is not zero.
D is wrong: The area of the unit disc is π, not 2π.

quizzes.title: Triple Integrals, Flux, and the Theorems of Gauss and Stokes

questions.q: What is the volume element in spherical coordinates? [6.4]
options: ρ² sin φ dρ dφ dθ
ρ² cos φ dρ dφ dθ
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.4: Spherical coordinates use ρ, φ from the positive z axis, and θ; the element carries ρ² sin φ.
B is wrong: That resembles the cylindrical factor r, not the spherical one.
C is wrong: This omits the Jacobian factor.
D is wrong: With φ measured from the z axis, the factor is sin φ.

questions.q: What is the outward flux of F = x i + y j + z k through the sphere of radius a? [6.6]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.6: On the sphere F · n = a, and multiplying by the surface area 4π a² gives 4π a³.
B is wrong: That is the surface area alone; F · n equals a, not 1.
C is wrong: That is the volume of the ball, not the flux.
D is wrong: The field points outward everywhere, so the flux is positive.

questions.q: What does the divergence of a field measure at a point? [6.7]
options: The local rotation of the field
The net outflow per unit volume, how much the point acts as a source or sink
The work done around a closed loop
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.7: Divergence is ∂P/∂x + ∂Q/∂y + ∂R/∂z, the local rate of spreading out.
A is wrong: That is the curl.
C is wrong: That is circulation, a line integral.
D is wrong: That is the gradient of a scalar function.

questions.q: What does the divergence theorem state? [6.8]
options: The circulation around a curve equals the flux of the curl
The work along a path equals the potential difference
The divergence of a curl is always one
The outward flux through a closed surface equals the triple integral of the divergence over the solid inside
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.8: It is also called Gauss's theorem, and it underlies Gauss's law in Physics Two.
A is wrong: That is Stokes' theorem.
B is wrong: That is the gradient theorem for line integrals.
C is wrong: The divergence of a curl is always zero.

questions.q: What does Stokes' theorem relate? [6.10]
options: The flux through a closed surface and the divergence inside
The circulation around a closed curve and the flux of the curl through any surface bounded by it
A function on an interval and its endpoint values only
The gradient and the level surfaces
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.10: Orientations match by the right-hand rule, and in the plane it reduces to Green's theorem.
A is wrong: That is the divergence theorem.
C is wrong: That is the one-variable Fundamental Theorem.
D is wrong: That is a property of gradients, not Stokes' theorem.
